subject: Clearinghouse split: Invoice INV-2027-093 - multi-entity allocation
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@novamed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Finance <finance@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: INV-2027-093 — request for split allocation by legal entity

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the quick delivery on the April invoice (INV-2027-093). Our AP team reviewed and we need the invoice to be reissued as a split settlement across three legal entities so our ERP can post automatically. Required split: 60% to Novamed US (US entity), 30% to Novamed EU (EU VAT-registered entity), 10% to Novamed APAC.

We also need VAT handling for the EU line: reverse-charge (no VAT applied) but the invoice must include the EU VAT number for our records. Please include cost-center tags for each line so they map to our GL (we will provide tag IDs).

Attachments: I attached the original PDF of INV-2027-093 and POD for the shipment. Can you confirm whether Redwood can issue a single master invoice with split lines (one PDF) or if you need to issue three separate invoices? We prefer one PDF with separate lines if possible.

Timing: We need the corrected invoice by EOD Friday so our AR can process payment next week. Let me know if you need anything else.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Johnson
Head of Revenue Operations, Novamed Health
alice.johnson@novamed.com
+44 20 5555 1234
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@novamed.com>
Cc: Novamed Finance <finance@novamed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INV-2027-093 — request for split allocation by legal entity

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments.

Short answer: we can issue a single consolidated PDF that contains discrete invoice lines mapped to the three legal entities (master invoice with per-entity breakout). That format works for most ERPs and keeps a single payment flow while satisfying audit/VAT requirements. We do need the following to proceed:
- Legal entity names as you want them rendered on each invoice line (exact text)
- Tax / VAT IDs, and confirmation of reverse-charge for the EU entity
- GL / cost-center tag IDs you want on each invoice line (CSV preferred)
- Bank remit instructions for any split routing (if funds will be separated after receipt)

I've attached a small CSV template (proportional_alloc_template.csv) with the columns we need: line_description,amount_share_pct,entity_name,entity_tax_id,cost_center_tag. Can you populate and return?

Internal next steps (looping in Marissa and Karthik): Marissa — once we have the completed CSV and tax IDs, can billing reissue a consolidated invoice with three breakout lines and include the EU VAT reference and a note about reverse charge? Karthik — do we need any changes to ledger posting metadata for cross-entity reporting or to pass along an intercompany clearing GL for our finance team?

Alice — if you'd prefer three separate legal-entity invoices instead of a single PDF with breakout lines, we can do that too; tell us which you prefer.

I'll pause on issuing until we get the CSV + VAT IDs.

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0199

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INV-2027-093 — request for split allocation by legal entity

Thanks for the tag, Sean.

Quick internal note (billing ops): we can absolutely produce a single consolidated PDF with three breakout invoice lines. Proposed execution:
- Reissue invoice INV-2027-093-R1 (master) with Line 1 = 60% Novamed US, Line 2 = 30% Novamed EU (reverse charge note + EU VAT ID on line), Line 3 = 10% Novamed APAC.
- Each line will carry a cost_center meta field (we will print the cost-center ID in the invoice line description for your ERP mapping).
- Ledger posting: we'll create three bookkeeping lines against the appropriate intercompany clearing account; Marissa (me) will push the intercompany memo to finance.

Karthik — please confirm the GL: use clearing account 2100-IC (interco liability) for the EU and APAC portion and 1100-revenue for US portion, then internal recharges will be handled via our intercompany module. If you prefer a different clearing GL, let us know.

Alice — before we reissue, can you populate the CSV Sean attached and confirm the exact legal names and VATs? Also confirm whether Novamed prefers bank-split (multiple beneficiary accounts) or single beneficiary with downstream internal allocation (we default to single beneficiary unless you state otherwise).

I'll target issuance by Friday EOD conditional on receiving the CSV + VATs by Thursday EOB.

Attachments: I attached a quick sample of how the master invoice will look (visual mock, no PII).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Billing Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Cc: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INV-2027-093 — request for split allocation by legal entity

Marissa / Sean — thanks. Confirming GL guidance from finance: use 1100-REV for revenue recognition (US share), 2100-IC for intercompany clearing (EU + APAC share). For EU reverse charge we will set VAT amount to zero and include the field "Reverse Charge — Article 196" in the invoice notes.

One operational caveat: if Novamed requests separate beneficiary bank accounts at the point of invoice (i.e., payment split upstream), we need a signed amendment to our T&C for multi-beneficiary payments because it changes our receivables flow and collections SLA. If Novamed is okay with single beneficiary and downstream internal allocation, no amendment needed.

Action items we agreed on:
- Alice: return the completed proportional_alloc_template.csv with entity names, tax IDs, and cost center tags (by Thu EOB).
- Marissa: prepare draft INV-2027-093-R1 (master) with breakout lines and sample bookkeeping entries and circulate to Novamed for sign-off.
- Sean: confirm remit preference and whether Novamed needs separate PDFs per legal entity.

Karthik
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
